Position: Estimator / QS (Commercial)

Salary: $1,700 - $2,200 AUD a month

Working Hours & Conditions: Australian Hours

Holidays: Public holidays in AU

Role Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented Quantity Surveyor / Estimator with experience in commercial construction to support the preparation of tenders, cost estimates, and project pricing. This role is focused on analysing tender documentation, completing accurate material take-offs, and assisting with supplier pricing and procurement activities.

The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of commercial construction methodologies, excellent numerical skills, and experience working with estimating and procurement software.

Estimating & Tender Analysis (Primary Focus)

  • Review and analyse tender documentation, drawings, specifications, and scopes of work
  • Prepare detailed cost estimates for commercial construction projects
  • Conduct quantity take-offs and material measurements from plans and specifications
  • Identify project risks, exclusions, and cost considerations during tender review
  • Assist in preparing competitive and accurate tender submissions

Quantity Surveying & Cost Management

  • Complete accurate quantity calculations for materials, labour, and subcontractor scopes
  • Support budgeting, cost planning, and project feasibility assessments
  • Monitor and maintain estimating databases and pricing schedules
  • Assist with variation pricing and cost analysis where required

Supplier & Procurement Coordination

  • Source supplier and subcontractor pricing using ProcurePro
  • Obtain and compare quotations from suppliers and subcontractors
  • Assist with procurement planning and cost benchmarking
  • Maintain supplier databases and pricing records

Systems & Documentation

  • Prepare and maintain estimating records within BuildTrend
  • Ensure all project documentation is organised and accurately recorded
  • Support process improvements across estimating and procurement workflows
  • Assist with project handovers from estimating to delivery teams

Tools & Systems

  • BuildTrend (must / ideal)
  • ProcurePro (preferred)
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Commercial construction plans and estimating software

Requirements

    • Proven experience as a Quantity Surveyor, Estimator, or Cost Planner within commercial construction
    • Strong experience conducting material take-offs and quantity calculations
    • Ability to interpret architectural, structural, and engineering drawings
    • Strong analytical, numerical, and problem-solving skills
    • High attention to detail and commercial awareness
    • Ability to manage multiple tenders and deadlines simultaneously

Desirable

    • Experience with BuildTrend and/or EstimateOne
    • Experience working on commercial, industrial, or multi-residential projects
    • Understanding of Australian construction contracts and tender processes
    • Previous experience supporting procurement and supplier engagement

Additional Information

    • This is a high-priority role supporting a busy commercial construction team
    • Strong focus on tender scope analysis, quantity take-offs, and estimating accuracy
    • Opportunity to play a key role during a period of company growth and operational restructuring
    • Ideal for a commercially minded professional who enjoys detailed analysis and contributing to project success from the pre-construction stage

We are looking for a skilled and detail-oriented Estimator to join our project team within the real estate development and construction business, focusing on boutique hospitality assets.

In this role, you will be responsible for preparing cost estimates, managing budgets, analyzing project costs, and supporting procurement and contract administration throughout the project lifecycle. You should be able to work independently on day-to-day tasks, coordinate with the project team when needed, and deliver accurate reports and updates regularly. You will report to the Project Manager but collaborate closely with the entire design and construction team, including architects, interior designers, structural and MEP engineers, the FF&E procurement team, and client representatives.

This role will focus primarily on detailed cost estimations. Engagement in detailed estimation (AACE Class 3 and 2) will be around 80%, with involvement in early stages (AACE Class 5 and 4) up to 20%.

We expect you to be fluent in English and proficient in software such as Google Sheets, AutoCAD and Revit. Knowledge of procurement processes, tender documentation, and contract administration is also required.

To succeed in this role, you should have excellent analytical, communication, and presentation skills, be punctual, detail-oriented, and motivated to deliver accurate and timely results.

  • This is a full-time day role, with expected involvement of up to 40 hours per week.
  • This is a fully remote position
  • Utopia does not provide visa sponsorship or relocation packages for this position.
  • Conduct analysis to estimate materials, machinery, equipment and labour costs for construction projects.
  • Develop bills of quantities for construction activities.
  • Prepare cost estimates and budgets for construction projects.
  • Prepare detailed construction schedules for construction projects.
  • Review and challenge proposals from contractors, subcontractors and suppliers.
  • Prepare and submit progress reports and variations to stakeholders.
  • Quote materials, machinery, equipment, labour and services.
  • Resolve any disputes related to costs or contracts.

Who you will work with

  • Reporting to:
    • Project manager in charge of overall project performance: Close relation to ensure budget and schedule compliance.
  • Working closely with:
    • Internally:
      • Project design coordinator in charge of the development of architectural and interior design.
      • Finance team in charge of approving expenses and giving advice on financial matters.
      • Legal team in charge of overseeing all legal affairs of the company.
      • Construction team according to the construction strategy to be defined for each project.
    • Externally:
      • Local architect of record company in charge of developing detailed architectural and engineering design, planning plans, construction documentation and site supervision.
      • Local legal consultants when needed to advise on legal matters.
      • Contractors/subcontractors/suppliers according to the construction strategy for each project.

Key Role Outcomes

  • Accurate and clear bill of quantities and supporting documentation according to design and development phases.
  • Accurate cost and time estimates according to design and development phases.
  • Timely quoting of materials and subcontracts.
  • Clear communication and resolution of cost-related issues.

Requirements

  • Education
    • Bachelor's degree in estimation, quantity surveying, civil engineering, architecture or other related field.
  • Work Experience
    • Proven experience as an estimator in construction projects (+6 years).
    • Proven experience as an estimator in high-end hospitality/residential projects (+3 years).
    • Proven experience estimating budgets for construction projects over $20M USD.
    • Proficiency in relevant software (e.g., Excel, Google Sheets, Revit, AutoCAD).
    • Proven built network of industry connections and relationships with contractors, subcontractors and suppliers.

Benefits

  • Global project exposure — contribute to luxury hospitality developments across Europe, Africa, and Latin America.
  • A truly international team — collaborate across cultures, disciplines, and time zones with people bringing diverse perspectives and expertise.
  • High ownership environment — we value initiative, independent thinking, and people who take responsibility for meaningful work.
  • Growth opportunities — as we scale, we create new roles internally and support team members in expanding their scope and responsibilities.
  • Flexible collaboration formats — depending on the role, we offer fully remote, hybrid, and on-site opportunities designed to support effective collaboration and individual productivity.
  • Work on projects from concept to realization — contribute across the full architectural and engineering journey, from early design through execution.
  • Cross-disciplinary collaboration — engage directly with interiors, architecture, landscape, construction, and operations teams from the earliest project stages.

Position: Quantity Surveyor

Salary: Php 70,000 to Php 80,000

Working Hours: Aligned with NZ Business Hours

Work Type: Independent Contractor

ABOUT THE COMPANY:

The company is an established New Zealand civil construction and earthworks business with over 35 years of industry excellence. Servicing residential and commercial projects across Auckland, the North Shore, and surrounding regions, the company specialises in comprehensive site development—including bulk earthworks, excavation, drainage infrastructure, site preparation, retaining systems, foundations, concrete works, and residential subdivisions. Backed by a rapidly expanding project pipeline, the company is committed to high-quality delivery, operational efficiency, and sustainable business growth.

ROLE OVERVIEW:

Working directly alongside the Company Director and Project Manager, the Quantity Surveyor / Civil Estimator will spearhead internal estimating and tendering operations. The primary objective is to take full ownership of quantity takeoffs, detailed Bills of Quantities (BOQs), cost schedules, and tender preparation.

This critical role is focused on driving turnaround efficiency, clearing enquiry backlogs, and transitioning externally subcontracted estimating functions directly in-house. It offers an exceptional long-term opportunity for a proactive professional with direct exposure to New Zealand or Australian construction standards to manage projects autonomously with high accuracy.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

Quantity Surveying & Cost Estimation:

  • Prepare precise quantity takeoffs, BOQs, and first-principle cost estimates from structural, architectural, and civil drawings.
  • Accurately calculate costs for plant, machinery, materials, direct labour, and specialist subcontractor packages.
  • Compile and present competitive, professional tender packages and client quotations across residential and civil scopes.
  • Audit project drawings and specifications to pinpoint scope ambiguities, discrepancies, constructability risks, and potential variations.
  • Maintain clean, auditable estimating databases, rate libraries, and project documentation.

Civil Earthworks & Siteworks Pricing:

  • Price diverse scopes including site clearing, excavation, cut/fill balancing, grading, levelling, and compaction.
  • Estimate residential and commercial drainage packages, including stormwater and wastewater retention/detention infrastructure.
  • Cost underground service trenching, piling, drilling, foundations, and retaining wall installations.
  • Formulate accurate estimates for concrete flatwork, paving, driveways, residential subdivisions, and exterior works.

Project & Commercial Coordination:

  • Liaise with the Director and Project Manager to align on commercial strategy, margins, and pipeline priorities.
  • Solicit, review, and benchmark supplier and subcontractor bids to guarantee cost certainty.
  • Proactively follow up on RFIs, missing design documentation, and addenda.
  • Support post-tender negotiations, value engineering exercises, and initial client correspondence.

Requirements

  • Proven track record as a Quantity Surveyor, Civil Estimator, or Construction Cost Planner.
  • Minimum of 2 years of direct experience pricing projects within the Australian or New Zealand construction sectors.
  • Solid technical proficiency across civil earthworks, drainage, infrastructure siteworks, and residential structures.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently read, interpret, and mark up civil, architectural, and structural plans.
  • Hands-on proficiency with estimating software (Buildxact or Bluebeam).
  • Advanced capabilities in Microsoft Excel for complex cost modelling.
  • Exceptional command of written and spoken English, paired with clear communication skills.
  • Ability to work aligned with New Zealand Business Hours (NZST/NZDT).

PREFERRED:

  • Direct background working with New Zealand civil contractors and residential developers.
  • Working knowledge of New Zealand Standards (NZS 3910), regional consenting norms, council requirements, and current local supplier rates.
  • Practical experience utilizing Bluebeam Revu for digital takeoffs.
  • Combined experience across civil siteworks and residential superstructure builds.

What You’ll Bring:

  • End-to-End Ownership: A self-starter mindset capable of managing the estimating process from preliminary drawings through to final submission with minimal oversight.
  • Analytical Rigour: An eagle eye for detail that identifies omissions in plan sets, pricing hazards, and margin-optimisation opportunities.
  • Velocity & Organization: The capability to manage multiple active tenders simultaneously without sacrificing numerical accuracy.
  • Commercial Reliability: A dependable professional approach focused on punctuality, active communication, and long-term commitment to a close-knit, highly skilled construction leadership team.

​​Looking for Filipino (Philippines-based) candidates

Job Role: Senior Estimator & Quantity Surveyor

Compensation Range:$2000-$2500 AUD / Month

Engagement Type:Independent Contractor

Work Schedule: 40 hours per week, aligned with Perth business hours (same time zone as Manila).

Who We Are: At Hunt St we help Australian companies directly hire top 5% remote talent in the Philippines. You will be hired directly by the client, typically as an independent contractor. We are not an outsourcing agency. All of our roles are 100% remote so you'll be able to work from home.

Who The Client Is:

A full-service design and renovation firm based in Perth, Australia, specializing in luxury home transformations. With nearly two decades of experience, the team is dedicated to crafting timeless, personalized, and refined spaces that elevate and reflect each client's lifestyle. Their philosophy blends creativity with meticulous craftsmanship, intentionally limiting the number of projects taken on each year to ensure every detail receives focused attention.

Role Overview:

The Senior Estimator & Quantity Surveyor will take ownership of construction estimating for
high-end residential renovation projects, ensuring accurate pricing, comprehensive quantity
take-offs and effective cost control throughout the project lifecycle.

This role requires substantial experience working with Australian residential builders and a
strong understanding of local construction practices, trade scopes, material costs and
subcontractor pricing. The ideal candidate is proactive, commercially minded and highly
organised, with the ability to manage the quoting pipeline, identify potential risks early, and
deliver reliable cost estimates with minimal supervision. The Directors and Project Director
remain part of all key decisions, and the Directors review each estimate before it is finalised.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Construction Estimating

  • Prepare accurate quantity take-offs and trade-by-trade estimates from architectural, interior design, structural and joinery drawings and specifications.
  • Build an RFQ package for each trade, including scope markups, site photos and product information.
  • Send RFQs to subcontractors and suppliers, follow them up, compare quotations and build the estimate from the returned pricing.
  • Price high-end finishes, including custom joinery, natural stone, large-format tiling, wet areas, cladding and premium fixtures.
  • Identify documentation gaps and inconsistencies, and raise Requests for Information (RFIs) where needed.
  • Identify cost risks, provisional sums, exclusions and value engineering opportunities before the price goes to the client.
  • Cross-check every estimate through Claude.
  • Revise estimates and markups based on the Directors' on-site review and feedback.
  • Lead an internal pricing meeting with the Directors to review the estimate before they meet the client.
  • Email clients regarding pricing questions when required and review client meeting transcripts afterwards to identify pricing changes.
  • The Estimator is not required to attend client meetings.

2. Project Set-Up

  • Build the job in Buildertrend once the contract is signed, including the master budget, cost codes and purchase orders issued with the relevant subcontractor quote, markup and take-off.
  • Save markups in one folder per trade so the Director (Project or Construction Manager), Project Director and relevant trade can access them.
  • Hand over a clear cost breakdown, risk items and allowance schedules to the Project Director.

3. Variations and Cost Control

  • Price variations within 24 hours of the request, subject to trade pricing, following the same process used for quoting: scope, photos and markups, trade pricing, then the client variation price.
  • Price each variation in Buildertrend Change Orders, including line items against the job's cost codes, trade quote references, margin, GST and variation fee.
  • Complete the Change Order when the change is complex or the Project Director hands it over, ready for the Director's review before it goes to the client.
  • Re-price items when clients upgrade or downgrade selections.
  • Check actual costs against each variation's cost codes once it is included in the budget.
  • Track costs against the budget and update the forecast to complete every fortnight in coordination with the Project Director and Accounts Manager.

4. Pricing Data and Claude

  • Maintain the rate library for materials, labour and trades, reviewing it at least every six months and after major supplier price changes.
  • Load each final estimate back into Claude to improve early design estimates.
  • Manage the quoting pipeline, including live quotes, deadlines, follow-ups and next actions.

Key Deliverables

  • Accurate quantity take-offs, detailed estimates, and timely quotations.
  • Reliable concept-stage cost plans and budget estimates.
  • Proactively managed quoting pipeline and supplier follow-ups.
  • Accurate cost tracking, variation pricing, and budget reporting.
  • Well-maintained pricing records and clear communication of project risks.

Requirements

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • At least five years of estimating and quantity surveying experience working with Australian residential builders, including high-end renovations. This is a non-negotiable requirement.
  • Sound knowledge of Perth and Western Australian trade, supplier and material pricing.
  • Experience pricing custom joinery, natural stone, large-format tiling, wet areas, cladding and premium fixtures.
  • Proficiency in digital take-off software such as Cubit, Buildxact, Databuild, Bluebeam or similar.
  • Strong knowledge of the National Construction Code (NCC), Australian Standards, trade scopes and construction sequencing.
  • Advanced Excel skills.
  • Clear written and spoken English, with confidence communicating with clients by email, designers, suppliers and subcontractors.
  • Strong organisational skills and a proactive approach to managing competing deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while collaborating effectively with a small team.

Highly Regarded

  • Experience using Buildertrend, including estimates, purchase orders and Change Orders.
  • Experience using AI tools such as Claude in estimating.
  • Experience in variation pricing, job costing and cost-to-complete forecasting.
  • Familiarity with HIA contracts and a design-and-construct environment.
  • Experience using Xero.

Work Arrangement & Expectations:

This is a remote role that will be set up as an independent contractor engagement.

To ensure alignment and transparency, successful candidates will be expected to:

  • Disclose any existing ongoing roles or client work
  • Reflect this engagement on their LinkedIn profile (clearly marked as “Independent Contractor”)

  • Be a role model that drives a one business culture that achieves great outcomes by striking the right balance for our people, clients, stakeholders, and society.

  • Construction consultancy experience is strongly preferred.
  • Good knowledge of construction industry technical matters, such as different procurement routes, value management, and value engineering.
  • Excellent communication skills.

Contractors bleed margin on every project.

Shape fixes this once and for all.

Shape is the only platform simple enough for field teams to adopt instantly, yet powerful enough to drive real commercial outcomes.
